tasks.title: Diagnose, then fix, the floor reorder drop defect
acceptance: DIAGNOSIS BEFORE FIX. Before any production edit, the report states the mechanism of the defect and names the single observation that discriminates it from the other candidates in contract C1 section 5. Naming candidate #1 (ShowDragPlaceholder mutating FloorListContainer.Children from inside the DragOver handler) without a discriminating observation does NOT satisfy this; neither does a fix landed before a diagnosis is written. The diagnosis names the file and the line the mechanism lives at, and says whether those line numbers are pre-edit or post-edit.

The three theories already refuted in contract C1 section 5 are not re-opened. In particular the report must not propose setting DataPackageOperation.Move: contract C1 section 4 records that Copy is the ONLY non-None member MAUI's DataPackageOperation enum has. If new evidence overturns a refuted theory, the report states that evidence rather than asserting the theory.

HUMAN OBSERVATION, run by the orchestrator with the user and NOT by this task. The report contains a numbered observation protocol the orchestrator can execute unchanged: the build command, 'open Test Dungeon #1 (11 floors), maximize at 1920x1080 so all floors fit and no scrollbar is present', 'drag FloorDragHandle on floor 3 onto the card of floor 7', and the five things the observer must look at and report: (a) does the SOURCE card become invisible at drag start, which is DragStarted setting Opacity 0 and is the proof OnDragStarting fired; (b) does the TARGET card show the gold DragOver stroke; (c) does a placeholder gap appear; (d) after release, is the order 1,2,4,5,6,7,3,... as expected; (e) is any 'Could not reorder the floors' line shown. THIS CRITERION IS MET when the observer reports (d) changed to the expected order and (e) showed nothing. It is NOT met by any in-process test. THE OBSERVATION IS RUN BY THE ORCHESTRATOR WITH THE USER (Gate 2, escalation E5 resolved). This task does not run it and must not report it as run. The task's deliverable is the protocol itself, stated precisely enough that the orchestrator can execute it unchanged; the criterion is judged by dir-reviewer FROM THE OBSERVATION TRANSCRIPT the orchestrator hands it alongside the diff. If no transcript is supplied, this criterion is UNDETERMINED, not met.

A regression test exists over the seam the diagnosis identifies, and is SHOWN ABLE TO FAIL by one of the two routes: a red step (the named command, run before the fix existed, with the observed failure quoted), or a demonstrated discrimination (the diagnosed defect re-injected into the fixed code, the named command, and the failure it produced). The same run must include a NAMED CONTROL test that stays GREEN, and the report names it. An injection in which the control also fails is an inert injection and does not satisfy this criterion. 'Verified by inspection' satisfies neither route.

If the diagnosis is that no in-process test can reach the mechanism because it is a platform gesture-routing fact, the report states that with the evidence for it, and the previous criterion is met instead by a test over the drop DECISION logic covering at least four of contract C1 section 1's rows: missing 'FloorId' key, unparseable value, drop-on-self, and the success row asserting ReorderFloorCommand receives (draggedFloorId, targetFloor.Number) and not an index. That substitute test must still be shown able to fail by one of the two routes above, and must NOT be a source-text, grep, or line-number assertion.

Contract C1 sections 1 and 2 hold after the change: all five tabulated error cases behave as written (four silent returns, one ErrorMessage of exactly $"Could not reorder the floors: {exception.Message}"), and _editor.SelectedFloorId is set before the await. The report states how many production call sites of ReorderFloorCommand exist after the change and names the command it counted them with; if the number is not 2, it says why.

Any change to a line contract C1 marks FROZEN is escalated to the orchestrator rather than made. Any change to a line marked T1-MUTABLE is stated explicitly in the report, because T2, T3 and T5 are dispatched against the value this task leaves behind.

`dotnet build src/DungeonMaster.sln` reports `0 Warning(s), 0 Error(s)`, and the report quotes that line. IDE0055 is a build error in this repository and every tracked file is CRLF: edits are made with the edit tools only. `sed -i`, `>` redirection over a tracked file, and any other whole-file rewrite are forbidden here because they silently convert line endings and turn the next build red.

`dotnet test src/DungeonMaster.App.Tests/DungeonMaster.App.Tests.csproj --no-build` and `dotnet test src/DungeonMaster.Tests/DungeonMaster.Tests.csproj --no-build` both report 0 failed, and the report quotes the passed/failed/total line from each.

tasks.title: MASTER-164: make the expand toggle a keyboard-focusable glyph Button with a pinned footprint
acceptance: MEASURE THE BASELINE FIRST, before any edit. The report records the rendered Height of the floor card's header Grid and of the whole floor card, as observed in the running application at a maximized 1920x1080 window with Test Dungeon #1 (11 floors). The report names the instrument: either temporary in-process instrumentation that writes the numbers to a file and is reverted before the task ends, or an orchestrator-run human observation whose protocol the report contains. A baseline argued from the XAML rather than observed does not satisfy this.

ExpandToggle is a Button, not a Label, and satisfies every row of contract C3 section 1: Transparent BackgroundColor, BorderWidth 0, Margin 0, the same two glyphs still flipped in ApplyExpanded alongside the SemanticProperties.Description rewrite, a visual glyph box of about 16x23, and a hit area of at least 23x23 reached by Padding rather than by growing the glyph. AutomationId FloorExpandToggle is preserved exactly (contract C2 section 1).

REVERTING THE ELEMENT TYPE IS A BUILD ERROR, not a silent regression. The code-behind references at least one Button-only member of ExpandToggle. The task demonstrates this by temporarily changing the XAML element back to Label, running `dotnet build src/DungeonMaster.sln`, quoting the compiler error id and message it produced, then restoring the Button. This is the demonstrated-discrimination evidence for this task and it must be actually run, not described.

THE HEIGHT INVARIANT OF CONTRACT C3 SECTION 2 HOLDS: the header row's rendered height and the floor card's rendered height are the same after this task as the baseline measured in criterion 1, measured by the same instrument at the same window size. A header-row height change is the exact cost the user declined this remedy for at sub-session 5c's escalation E5, so any change at all fails this criterion and is escalated rather than accepted.

MUST-RUN QUESTION 1 (contract C3 section 3): the report answers, from an observation and not from the API surface, whether MinimumWidthRequest/MinimumHeightRequest actually override the WinUI default Button minimum on Windows, quoting the rendered Width and Height of ExpandToggle in the running application and naming how those numbers were obtained. If they do NOT override it, the task ESCALATES to the orchestrator rather than silently substituting a different mechanism.

HUMAN OBSERVATION, run by the orchestrator with the user and NOT by this task. The report contains a numbered protocol: launch, open Test Dungeon #1, press Tab repeatedly from app start and report the ordered list of what the focus ring lands on; then with the focus ring on the first floor's chevron press Space. The observer reports (a) whether the focus ring visibly reaches the chevron and within how many Tab presses, (b) whether Space expands the floor, and (c) whether '+ Add area' then becomes visible and reachable by a further Tab. THIS CRITERION IS MET when (a), (b) and (c) are all yes. At b3b1641 a 40-tab walk reached the chevron 0 times, which is the before-state this is measured against. THE OBSERVATION IS RUN BY THE ORCHESTRATOR WITH THE USER (Gate 2, escalation E5 resolved). This task does not run it and must not report it as run. The task's deliverable is the protocol itself, stated precisely enough that the orchestrator can execute it unchanged; the criterion is judged by dir-reviewer FROM THE OBSERVATION TRANSCRIPT the orchestrator hands it alongside the diff. If no transcript is supplied, this criterion is UNDETERMINED, not met.

NONE of the four things contract C3 section 4 forbids is done: no layout, Border, Grid or card body is made focusable via IsTabStop/TabIndex/Focus (absent from MAUI 10's public API and deliberately removed in MAUI 9); no MAUI Community Toolkit Expander is introduced; the card-body TapGestureRecognizer stays, because the chevron's sub-minimum visual is sanctioned only by that redundancy; and FloorBorder acquires no SemanticProperties.Description, which on iOS/Mac Catalyst would hide the three header buttons from VoiceOver. Verified by reading the diff.

`dotnet build src/DungeonMaster.sln` reports `0 Warning(s), 0 Error(s)` and the report quotes that line. Edits are made with the edit tools only: tracked files are CRLF and IDE0055 is a build error, so `sed -i` or any whole-file rewrite turns the next build red.
`dotnet test src/DungeonMaster.Tests/DungeonMaster.Tests.csproj --no-build` and `dotnet test src/DungeonMaster.App.Tests/DungeonMaster.App.Tests.csproj --no-build` both report 0 failed, quoted.

tasks.title: MASTER-163: move the floor drag handle clear of the WinUI overlay scrollbar gutter
acceptance: MEASURE THE GUTTER BEFORE RESERVING IT. The report states the WinUI overlay scrollbar's width in device-independent units as OBSERVED on this machine in the running application, and names how it was obtained. A reservation sized from a remembered or documented number, with no observation, does not satisfy this criterion. Note that Platforms/Windows/App.xaml.cs:124-136 overrides scrollbar COLOUR only and reserves nothing.

The drag handle's right edge clears that gutter. The remedy is either reserving the gutter (right padding on the ScrollView content or a right margin on the card Border, which at b3b1641 is Margin="0,0,0,4" with ZERO right margin) or moving the handle out of Grid.Column 4. The report states which was chosen, the reserved width, and why that width follows from the measurement in criterion 1.

CONTRACT C3 SECTION 5: the header row's rendered height and the floor card's rendered height do not change. A WIDTH change is permitted and expected; a remedy that adds a row, wraps the handle below the row, or otherwise grows the card vertically fails this criterion. Measured in the running application by the instrument T2's report names, and the number is quoted.

CONTRACT C1 SECTION 3: the DragGestureRecognizer stays hosted on the drag-handle Label and nowhere else, with the handler names OnDragStarting and OnDropCompleted unchanged, and AutomationId FloorDragHandle preserved exactly (contract C2 section 1). This task makes a layout change and nothing else to the reorder path. Verified by reading the diff.

HUMAN OBSERVATION, run by the orchestrator with the user and NOT by this task. The report contains a numbered protocol with THREE steps. STEP 1 (drag handle): open Test Dungeon #1 (11 floors) in a window SMALL ENOUGH THAT THE SIDEBAR SCROLLS and the overlay scrollbar is present (the 1920x1080 maximized case fits all 11 and is the wrong configuration for this test), then attempt to grab the drag handle of the third floor card. The observer reports whether the handle was grabbed on the first attempt without the pointer catching the scrollbar. THIS CRITERION IS MET when the answer is yes. The before-state it is measured against is measurement.md section 2: 'the drag started; the scrollbar did not block it, but made the handle very difficult to grab'. STEP 2 (MASTER-175 cursor): hover the pointer over an EXPANDED floor's area row, over the row's body and not over its notebook or delete button, and report whether the hand cursor appears. Cursor shape cannot be read by any automated instrument -- HandCursorBehavior sets WinUI's non-public ProtectedCursor, which no other process can read, and screenshots do not capture the Windows cursor (HANDOFF-session-6.md:104) -- so a human is the only instrument for step 2 and no substitute is accepted. STEP 2 IS MET when the observer reports the hand cursor over the area row body. STEP 3 (missed drop, escalation E6): repeat step 1's drag but RELEASE THE POINTER BETWEEN two floor cards -- on the gap, not on a card. The observer reports whether anything at all happens: a reorder, an error line, or any other feedback. STEP 3 IS MET when the miss produces an OBSERVABLE OUTCOME rather than nothing -- either the floor reorders anyway (shape a) or a message is shown (shape b). At b3b1641 the answer is that nothing happens at all, which is the before-state step 3 is measured against. THE OBSERVATION IS RUN BY THE ORCHESTRATOR WITH THE USER (Gate 2, escalation E5 resolved). This task does not run it and must not report it as run. The task's deliverable is the protocol itself, stated precisely enough that the orchestrator can execute it unchanged; the criterion is judged by dir-reviewer FROM THE OBSERVATION TRANSCRIPT the orchestrator hands it alongside the diff. If no transcript is supplied, this criterion is UNDETERMINED, not met.

THE SEVERITY DIRECTION IS UPWARD, NOT DOWNWARD (escalation E6, and this REVERSES what this task was told at Gate 2). The report must state in one sentence that MASTER-163 is this session's PRIMARY defect. The reorder feature ITSELF works end to end when the drop lands on a target: the orchestrator observed it with the user on 2026-09-11 at 1920x1080 with all 11 floors visible and NO scrollbar rendered -- source card vanished at drag start, target showed the gold DragOver stroke, a placeholder gap appeared, the order changed as expected, no error line, and the database confirmed the move persisted (Guest Rooms 3 to 7); transcript at observations/T1-reorder.md. So what fails is REACHING the drop target, and when the drop misses it fails SILENTLY -- which is why the feature reads as broken. The entry's literal 'cannot be performed at all' clause is still false and the report says so, but the correction is that the real defect is WORSE than ergonomics, not milder than a blocked feature. A report that describes this task as fixing awkward ergonomics, or that repeats the pre-E6 framing of a severity coming down, FAILS this criterion.

A DROP THAT MISSES EVERY DROP TARGET NO LONGER FAILS SILENTLY (escalation E6; this is the fix for what was mistaken for a separate reorder defect, and it is folded into this task rather than filed as a peer defect). At b3b1641 `FloorListContainer` is a bare `VerticalStackLayout` at src/DungeonMaster.App/Views/DungeonDetailPage/DungeonDetailPage.xaml:668 carrying NO `DropGestureRecognizer` -- that file declares none at all -- so a drop landing between cards, or on any space no handler owns, is discarded with no handler, no error and no trace. TWO SHAPES ARE ACCEPTABLE and this task chooses ON EVIDENCE, stating in the report which it chose and why: (a) `FloorListContainer` accepts drops, so a near-miss still resolves to a target and reorders; or (b) a missed drop is SURFACED to the user rather than discarded. WHAT MUST END IS THE SILENT DISCARD -- the mechanism is this task's to decide and this criterion does not prescribe it. OWNERSHIP, CORRECTED AT ESCALATION E8 (the Gate 2 wording here was a decomposition error and said no ownership change was needed, which was FALSE): `FloorListContainer` is declared in `DungeonDetailPage.xaml`, which this task already owned, but a XAML event handler resolves against `DungeonDetailPage.xaml.cs` -- T4's file -- and the command-bound alternative needs `DungeonDetailViewModel`, owned by nobody. This task could not satisfy this criterion from its own files. The user has granted it `src/DungeonMaster.App/Views/DungeonDetailPage/DungeonDetailPage.xaml.cs` and `src/DungeonMaster.App.Core/Editor/FloorReorder*.cs`; both are now in this task's owns set, and both carry a direct dependsOn edge (T4->T3 and T3->T1) so no concurrent dispatch is possible. Writing outside those globs is still an ownership violation and is still escalated, never done. SHAPE (a) IS THE ONE BEING BUILT, per the re-dispatch: a `DropGestureRecognizer` on `FloorListContainer`, nearest-item resolution by vertical midpoint in a new pure function in `App.Core/Editor/FloorReorder*.cs`, reusing `FloorReorderDrop.Decide` and the existing `ReorderFloorCommand` call shape. Contract C1 section 4's drop-target count is therefore THREE, amended there, and this task's report states the count it left behind because T5 and T6 are dispatched against it. The nearest-item resolution is a PURE FUNCTION and is where this criterion's automated test lives -- that seam exists, so the structural-half waiver below does not apply to it. STRUCTURAL HALF: `dotnet build src/DungeonMaster.sln` reports `0 Warning(s), 0 Error(s)`, plus an automated test over whatever seam the chosen shape introduces, SHOWN ABLE TO FAIL by a red step or a demonstrated discrimination with a NAMED GREEN CONTROL in the same run; if the chosen shape is reachable only through platform gesture routing and no in-process seam exists, the report says so WITH EVIDENCE and the structural half is waived. OBSERVABLE HALF: STEP 3 of the orchestrator-run observation pass in the criterion above, and nothing else.

MASTER-175 IS FIXED HERE, NOT MERELY FILED (Gate 2 decision, resolving coverage gap U4). AreaSidebarItem's card body -- the root `Border x:Name="ItemBorder"` at src/DungeonMaster.App/Controls/AreaSidebarItem/AreaSidebarItem.xaml:12-13, which carries `TapGestureRecognizer Tapped="OnItemTapped"` at :138 and `HoverOrLongPressBehavior` at :141-145 but NO `HandCursorBehavior` at all -- gains a `HandCursorBehavior`, attached inside the existing `Border.Behaviors` block alongside `HoverOrLongPressBehavior`, matching the attachment already present on the floor card body at FloorSidebarItem.xaml:88. The file's only two existing attachments, the Buttons at :111 and :131, both stay. AutomationId `AreaRow` at :13 is preserved exactly. THIS IS A BEHAVIOR ATTACHMENT ONLY: no layout, no sizing, no gesture and no visual-state change to that control, verified by reading the diff. Its structural half is checked by the diff plus `dotnet build src/DungeonMaster.sln` reporting `0 Warning(s), 0 Error(s)`; its OBSERVABLE half is met by STEP 2 of the orchestrator-run observation pass in the criterion above, because cursor shape is unreadable cross-process. This is ABSENCE being closed, not the inertness MASTER-165 alleges -- measurement.md section 2 observed the hand cursor working on all three floor-card configurations, so the behavior itself is sound and only the attachment was missing.

HANDOFF TO T5: the report states the exact durable fact T5 is to freeze as an Appium assertion, as a single sentence with numbers in it, of the form 'FloorDragHandle's right edge is at least N device-independent units left of the sidebar scroll viewport's right edge'. T5 owns the assertion; this task owns the number. Without this sentence T5 has nothing to assert against.
`dotnet build src/DungeonMaster.sln` reports `0 Warning(s), 0 Error(s)`, quoted. Edits made with the edit tools only: tracked files are CRLF and IDE0055 is a build error.
`dotnet test src/DungeonMaster.Tests/DungeonMaster.Tests.csproj --no-build` and `dotnet test src/DungeonMaster.App.Tests/DungeonMaster.App.Tests.csproj --no-build` both report 0 failed, quoted.

tasks.title: MASTER-166: measure whether the optimistic ghost frame is reachable, then order the clear after the refresh
acceptance: MEASURE FIRST. The report establishes whether the awaited AddAreaWithOutlineCommand write returns inside one frame interval. It states: the command run, the number of samples, the min/median/max in milliseconds, and the frame interval compared against (16.7ms at 60Hz, and the report says what refresh rate it assumed). A single sample is not a measurement and does not satisfy this criterion.

THE APPARATUS CAVEAT IS STATED. The measurement is taken against a FILE-BACKED SQLite database, not src/DungeonMaster.Tests/Infrastructure/Persistence/SqliteInMemoryTestBase.cs's in-memory one: an in-memory write understates real local-database latency and answers a different question. If the task measures in-memory anyway because a file-backed harness is out of reach, the report says so plainly and labels the number as a LOWER BOUND, not as the answer.

THE CONCLUSION IS STATED AS WHAT IT IS. If the write returns inside one frame interval, the report says the ghost frame is structurally unreachable AT THIS MEASURED LATENCY — as a measurement, not as a proven cause of sub-session 5c's negative 45-frame capture. A report that presents a consistent observation as a proven cause fails this criterion. The audit record itself already concedes at 00-master-index.md:572 that 'a negative capture is not proof'.

THE ORDERING CHANGE SHIPS REGARDLESS of what the measurement shows, because it is justified independently: at b3b1641 ClearGhostAreas() runs before `await RefreshFloorAsync()` in FinishDrawing, leaving a window in which neither the ghost nor the persisted area is on screen. After this task, ClearGhostAreas() runs AFTER `await RefreshFloorAsync()`.

THE SECOND SITE IS IN SCOPE: the optimistic area-move path has the identical add-invalidate-await-clear shape, with ClearPendingMoveOffsets() before `await RefreshFloorAsync()`. Either the same ordering is applied there, or the report records the measured reason the two sites differ. Silently fixing one and not mentioning the other fails this criterion.

THE PLACE-TOOL GHOST OBJECT IS UNTOUCHED. src/DungeonMaster.App/Graphics/FloorMapDrawable.cs:457-467 is a live cursor-follow preview and a different mechanism; it is not this entry and must not be folded in. This task owns no file under src/DungeonMaster.App/Graphics/, so any edit there is also an ownership violation. Verified by reading the diff.

AN AUTOMATED TEST FAILS IF THE CLEAR RUNS BEFORE THE REFRESH. It asserts the recorded ORDER of the operations over a seam that records call order — NOT the source text, NOT a line number, and NOT a wall-clock duration (the test discipline forbids tests that depend on the clock, and a timing assertion here would be intermittent). It is SHOWN ABLE TO FAIL by a red step or a demonstrated discrimination: the named command, the observed failure, and a NAMED CONTROL test in the same run that stays GREEN. An injection whose control also fails is inert and does not satisfy this criterion.

THE FOUR EXISTING GHOST TESTS STAY GREEN. `dotnet test src/DungeonMaster.App.Tests/DungeonMaster.App.Tests.csproj --no-build --filter "FullyQualifiedName~FloorMapDrawableStateTests|FullyQualifiedName~FloorMapDrawableAreaAlphaTests"` reports 0 failed, quoted with its totals. They are at FloorMapDrawableStateTests.cs:69-74, :79-84, :148-160 and FloorMapDrawableAreaAlphaTests.cs:96-110, and any claim that this entry is untested is wrong.

`dotnet build src/DungeonMaster.sln` reports `0 Warning(s), 0 Error(s)`, quoted, and `dotnet test src/DungeonMaster.Tests/DungeonMaster.Tests.csproj --no-build` reports 0 failed, quoted. Edits made with the edit tools only: tracked files are CRLF and IDE0055 is a build error.

tasks.title: Extend the Appium harness with floor-sidebar facts it can certainly assert
acceptance: READ src/DungeonMaster.App.UiTests/README.md BEFORE WRITING A LINE. The report reproduces its four-row prerequisite table (Appium server 3.7.0, Appium Windows driver windows@6.1.1, WinAppDriver 1.2.200902003-release, Appium.WebDriver client 8.3.2 pinned in Directory.Packages.props), states for each whether it is present on this machine, and names the check command from that table that it ran. A missing prerequisite is REPORTED, never worked around and never assumed present.

NO CRITERION OF THIS TASK DEPENDS ON AN AUTOMATED DRAG-AND-DROP REORDER SUCCEEDING. Contract C2 section 3 freezes this: synthetic mouse_event input was measured on 2026-09-11 not to initiate WinUI drag-and-drop at all (the source card stayed at full opacity, so OnDragStarting never fired), and whether Appium's W3C pointer actions can is UNPROVEN. The task MAY attempt pointer actions and MUST report the result as a finding either way; a failure there is a finding, not a failure of this task. The reorder's verification belongs to T1's human observation.

NEW FACTS ADDED, all four, each drawn only from contract C2 section 3's assertable set: (a) a tab-order walk from app start that reports the focused AutomationId after each Tab and asserts FloorExpandToggle appears in the sequence; (b) FloorExpandToggle's bounding rectangle is at least 23 by 23; (c) FloorDragHandle's right edge clears the sidebar scroll viewport's right edge by at least the number T3's report states (the orchestrator supplies T3's report at dispatch; if that sentence is absent, ESCALATE rather than inventing a number); (d) AddAreaButton is absent or offscreen while a floor is collapsed and present after FloorExpandToggle is activated.

EVERY NEW FACT HAS A NAMED CONTROL, following the experiment design this project's README already documents: a run in which everything fails cannot tell a detected defect from a broken apparatus. The report names, for each new fact, the control that stays green when that fact reddens, and demonstrates the asymmetry for at least one of them by disabling the driven step and quoting the resulting red/green split.

THE PROJECT ADDS NO AutomationId AND EDITS NO .xaml FILE, and is NOT added to src/DungeonMaster.sln — adding it makes a solution-wide `dotnet test` fail on every machine without the Appium tooling, which is the stated reason it sits outside the solution. Verified by the diff containing no file under src/DungeonMaster.App/ and no .sln change. If a needed AutomationId is not in contract C2 section 1's table, ESCALATE; do not add one.

`dotnet build src/DungeonMaster.App.UiTests/DungeonMaster.App.UiTests.csproj -v m` reports 0 warnings and 0 errors, quoted. This is the criterion that holds whether or not an Appium server is running.

RUN, WITH AN EXPLICIT STATED FALLBACK. `dotnet test src/DungeonMaster.App.UiTests/DungeonMaster.App.UiTests.csproj --logger "console;verbosity=detailed"` reports 0 failed, run by this task IF the Appium server, Windows Developer Mode and a built DungeonMaster.App.exe are all present. IF ANY PREREQUISITE IS ABSENT: the task reports WHICH one and BY WHAT CHECK it determined that, and this criterion is met instead by the ORCHESTRATOR running the same command with the prerequisites in place and handing the result to the reviewer. The fallback must be stated in the report as having been taken; a silent skip does not satisfy this criterion either way.

AFTER ANY RED RUN, `Get-Process DungeonMaster.App` is checked and leftovers are stopped. The README records one measured survivor with the driver already quit on 2026-09-04, so this is a known behaviour and not a hypothetical.

README.md is updated: the new facts are described in its 'What the tests do' section in the same form as the three existing ones, and the date these were proven is recorded alongside the 2026-09-04 row. Test names state the condition and the expected outcome; a name containing 'works' or 'is correct' names nothing and fails this criterion.

tasks.title: Correct the audit record and file the two new entries
acceptance: ALL ELEVEN CORRECTIONS in contract C4 section 3 are made, each as an inline amendment block in contract C4 section 5's format, each quoting the PREVIOUS WORDING VERBATIM and carrying a classification of MEASUREMENT ERROR, DRIFT or FALSIFIED. The precedent to copy is the three [AMENDED 6b-iii] blocks under MASTER-167. A correction that rewrites a claim without quoting what it replaced fails this criterion, because a reader who tested the old claim needs to see why it did not reproduce. CORRECTION 3 IS DIRECTIONAL AND THIS CRITERION IS NOT MET BY A DOWNWARD ONE. Per escalation E6, MASTER-163's severity is corrected UPWARD: the reorder feature works when the drop lands, so the defect is that reaching the target is impractical AND that a missed drop fails silently, which is strictly worse than the ergonomic framing this task was given at Gate 2. A T6 that writes a severity REDUCTION has FAILED this criterion even if it made the other ten corrections correctly, and dir-reviewer is to check the DIRECTION explicitly rather than only that an amendment block exists.

MASTER-174, MASTER-175 AND MASTER-176 ARE FILED at exactly those ids, appended with no renumbering of any existing entry, each with an index ROW and a DETAIL entry, per contract C4 section 1. MASTER-173 at 00-master-index.md:361 is the highest existing id, counted from that file. The note at 00-master-index.md:367 and the coverage-attestation bullet below it are extended to account for THREE more entries with no source record, rather than left silently stale.

MASTER-174 IS FILED AS THE SILENT-DISCARD DEFECT, NOT AS 'the reorder does not reorder' (escalation E6). That original characterisation is now KNOWN FALSE, and filing it would put a false claim into the very index this session exists to correct. The entry reads: A DROP THAT MISSES EVERY DROP TARGET IS DISCARDED SILENTLY, WITH NO ERROR AND NO FEEDBACK -- `FloorListContainer` (DungeonDetailPage.xaml:668) carries no `DropGestureRecognizer`. The entry MUST record the evidence that the reorder feature itself WORKS: the orchestrator's 2026-09-11 observation with the user at 1920x1080, all 11 floors visible, no scrollbar -- source card vanished at drag start, gold DragOver stroke on the target, placeholder gap, order changed as expected, no error line, and the database confirmed the move persisted (Guest Rooms 3 to 7) -- transcript at .dir-sdlc/sessions/2026-09-11-make-the-floor-sidebar-operable/observations/T1-reorder.md. It MUST also record that NONE of T1's four candidates is the mechanism, because in that configuration there is no defect. IT MUST NOT ASSERT THAT T1 FIXED A REORDER DEFECT: T1 delivered a behaviour-preserving refactor and the first tests ever to exist on the gesture-to-command path, and correctly declined to ship a speculative fix. T3's report, supplied by the orchestrator at dispatch, is the source for what shipped against the silent discard; if it is not supplied, ESCALATE.

MASTER-175's ENTRY DESCRIBES A DEFECT THIS SESSION CLOSED, NOT ONE LEFT OPEN (Gate 2 decision). T3 attached the missing HandCursorBehavior to AreaSidebarItem's root Border; the entry records the finding AND the fix, quoting T3's report, which the ORCHESTRATOR SUPPLIES AT DISPATCH. The entry must not read as an open item and must not read as a duplicate of MASTER-165: this one is ABSENCE (no behavior attached at all), MASTER-165 alleges INERTNESS (attached but ineffective) and is falsified. The STATUS is still left unwritten -- per contract C4 section 2 the orchestrator closes it with commit evidence at Gate 3 -- so the entry states what was found and what shipped, and carries no hash and no 'done'. If T3's report is not supplied, ESCALATE rather than describing a fix this task has not seen.
